title: RFMvsMeanDiff: Benchmarking Concept-Vector Extraction Methods Head-to-Head

original_idea.body:
# RFMvsMeanDiff: Benchmarking Concept-Vector Extraction Methods Head-to-Head

**Problem:** Beaglehole et al. use RFM-based concept extraction and report it beats baselines, but there is no accessible, apples-to-apples benchmark comparing common extraction methods (mean-difference CAA, logistic-regression probe, RFM) on the same safety concepts.

**Direction:** Implement 3 extraction methods on a shared open model and dataset, then compare them on probe detection AUC, steering effect size, and capability cost across 4-5 safety concepts. Produce a method-comparison table and note which method wins for detection vs for steering.

**Why it matters:** Method choice silently determines results; a shared comparison clarifies which extraction technique to trust for monitoring vs steering. Directly operationalizes the paper's RFM-vs-baseline claim in a reproducible, single-GPU way.

**Relevant context:** Beaglehole et al. report RFM aggregation gives SOTA concept detection. CAA (mean-diff) and linear-probe extraction are standard and open; scikit-learn covers all three for beginners.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible chain (better extraction yields trustworthy safety directions) but indirect, a gap to catastrophic-risk reduction.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Three standard extraction methods compared via scikit-learn, novice+mentor feasible.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused method-comparison table, but 4-5 concepts and 3 methods add breadth.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Mixed: useful but a methodological bake-off routinely done in labs.

low_compute.reasoning: Inference + standard extraction on shared model, single GPU.

novelty.reasoning: Extraction-method comparisons largely exist; mostly reproduction/synthesis.
